cues.en: You are about to learn one of the biggest secrets in the history of the world. It's a secret that has huge effects for everyone who lives on this planet. Most people can feel deep down that something isn't quite right with the world economy. But few know what it is. Gone are the days where a family can survive on just one paycheck. Every day it seems things are more and more out of control.
cues.zh: 你即将了解世界历史上最大的秘密之一。这个秘密对生活在这个星球上的每个人都有着巨大的影响。大多数人内心深处都能感觉到世界经济出了问题，但很少有人知道究竟是怎么回事。一个家庭只靠一份薪水就能生活的日子已经一去不复返了。情况似乎一天比一天失控。

cues.en: yet only one in a million understand why. You are about to discover the system that is ultimately responsible for most of the inequality in our world today. The powers that be do not want you to know about this, as this system is what has kept them at the top of the financial food chain for the last 100 years. Learning this will change your life because it'll change the choices that you make. If enough people learn it, it'll change the world because it'll change the system.
cues.zh: 然而百万人中只有一人明白其中的原因。你即将揭开当今世界绝大部分不平等现象的根源体系。当权者并不希望你知道这一切，因为正是这套体系让他们在过去的100年里稳坐金融食物链的顶端。了解这一点将改变你的人生，因为它会改变你的选择；如果有足够多的人了解它，它将改变世界，因为这套体系将被彻底颠覆。

cues.en: For this is the biggest hidden secret of money. Never in human history have so many been plundered by so few. And it's all accomplished through this, the biggest scam in the history of mankind. They say that money doesn't grow on trees. But the truth is that the modern banking system creates currency far faster than trees can grow. Most people don't have a clue how currency is created.
cues.zh: 因为这是货币最大的隐藏秘密。在人类历史上，从未有过极少数人能掠夺如此多的人。而这一切都是通过这个人类历史上最大的骗局实现的。人们常说钱不是树上长出来的，但事实是，现代银行体系创造货币的速度远比树木生长的速度要快。大多数人对货币究竟是如何创造出来的根本一无所知。

cues.en: Economists and bankers make it sound so complex that people think they can't understand it. But I'm going to strip our monetary system down to its essence so that you can see the scam behind the curtain and just how it affects you. Every modern society creates currency in pretty much the same way. But since the US dollar is the majority of the world's currency, I'm going to use the United States as our example. It all starts when some politician says, vote for me and I'll make sure the government provides you more free stuff than my opponent will.
cues.zh: 经济学家和银行家把它讲得极其复杂，让人以为自己根本搞不懂。但我会剥除货币体系的层层外衣，直击其本质，让你看清幕后的骗局以及它是如何影响你的。每个现代社会创造货币的方式都大同小异。但由于美元占据了全球货币的绝大部分，我将以美国为例。一切都始于某个政客说：“投我一票，我会确保政府给你比对手更多的免费福利。”

cues.en: But there's no such thing as a free lunch. So to provide that supposedly free stuff, the politicians vote for the country to spend more than its income. This is called deficit spending. To pay for that deficit spending, the Treasury borrows currency by issuing a bond. So what's a bond? If you think about it, a bond is really nothing but a glorified IOU. It's a pretty piece of paper with numbers printed on it that says
cues.zh: 但天下没有免费的午餐。因此，为了提供这些所谓的免费福利，政客们投票批准国家的支出超过其收入，这被称为赤字支出。为了支撑赤字支出，财政部通过发行债券来借入货币。那么什么是债券？仔细想想，债券本质上不过是一张包装得更体面的借条。它就是一张印着数字的漂亮纸片，上面写着：

cues.en: Loan me a trillion dollars today and I promise over a 10-year period I'm going to pay you back that trillion dollars plus interest. But what you need to understand is that Treasury bonds are our national debt. These glorified IOUs are to be paid back by you and I and our descendants through future taxation. Therefore, when the government issues a bond, it steals prosperity out of the future so that it can spend it today. The Treasury then holds a bond auction.
cues.zh: “今天借我一万亿美元，我保证在10年内连本带利还给你这一万亿。”但你需要明白的是，国债就是我们的国家债务。这些体面的借条，将来都要由你我以及我们的子孙后代通过未来的税收来偿还。因此，当政府发行债券时，它实际上是在透支未来的繁荣，好供今天挥霍。随后，财政部会举行一场国债拍卖。

cues.en: And the world's largest banks show up and compete to buy part of our national debt and make a profit on it by earning interest. You'll notice that as we move through this process, the big banks are there, taking a cut every step of the way. This isn't by chance, as you'll see shortly. Then, through a shell game called open market operations, the banks get to sell some of those bonds to the Federal Reserve at a profit. To pay for the bonds, the Federal Reserve opens up its big old checkbook and writes,
cues.zh: 全球最大的几家银行随即登场，竞相认购我们的部分国债，并通过赚取利息来牟利。你会注意到，在整个流程中，大银行无处不在，步步抽成。这绝非巧合，稍后你就会明白。接着，通过一场名为“公开市场操作”的障眼把戏，银行得以把其中一部分国债溢价卖给美联储。而为了买下这些国债，美联储翻开了它那本厚厚的支票簿，写下——

cues.en: bogus counterfeit checks that should bounce because they're drawn on an account that always has a zero balance. There isn't one penny in there. To quote from the Boston Federal Reserve, when you or I write a check, there must be sufficient funds in our account to cover that check. But when the Federal Reserve writes a check, there is no bank deposit on which that check is drawn. When the Federal Reserve writes a check, it is creating money.
cues.zh: ——写下一张张本该跳票的假支票，因为出票账户里的余额永远是零。里面连一分钱都没有。引用波士顿联储的话来说：你我开支票时，账户里必须有足够的资金来兑付；但当美联储开支票时，根本没有任何银行存款作为依托。美联储开支票的过程，就是在凭空创造货币。

cues.en: The Fed then hands those checks to the banks and at this point currency springs into existence. The banks then take that currency and buy more bonds at the next Treasury auction. But what is a check? A check is also an IOU. When you write a check, you're making a note that says, here's my IOU for cash. All you have to do is go to the bank and pick it up. Now it's very, very important that you understand this process because we're going to come back later and show you the devastating effect this has on you.
cues.zh: 美联储随后把这些支票交给银行，法币就在这一刻凭空诞生了。接着，银行拿着这些法币，在下一轮财政部国债拍卖中购买更多债券。但支票到底是什么？支票也是一种借条。你开支票时，其实就是写了张欠条说：“这是我换取现金的借据，去银行取就行”。搞懂这个流程极其重要，因为我们稍后会回过头来，向你展示它对你造成的毁灭性影响。

cues.en: The Treasury issues IOUs, bonds. The banks then buy those IOUs with currency. The Federal Reserve then writes IOUs, checks, and hands them to the banks in exchange for the Treasury's IOUs, the bonds. And currency is created. So what's really happening is the Federal Reserve and the Treasury are just swapping IOUs, using the banks as middlemen, and abracadabra presto currency magically springs into existence.
cues.zh: 财政部发行借条，也就是国债。银行用法币买下这些借条。美联储接着开出借条（也就是支票），交给银行以换取财政部的借条（国债）。于是法币诞生了。所以真相是：美联储和财政部不过是在互相交换借条，把银行当成中间人，然后“见证奇迹的时刻”——法币就这么凭空变了出来。

cues.en: This process repeats and repeats over and over again, enriching the banks and indenting the public by raising the national debt. The end result is that there's a buildup of bonds at the Federal Reserve and currency at the Treasury. This process is also where all paper currency comes from. The Federal Reserve and the government mistakenly call it base money because they didn't watch Episode 1 of this series and they don't know the difference between money and currency.
cues.zh: 这个过程周而复始、不断循环，一方面让银行赚得盆满钵满，另一方面推高国债让大众沦为债务奴隶。最终的结果是，国债在美联储越堆越高，法币在财政部越聚越多。所有纸币也正是由此而生。美联储和政府错误地将其称为“基础货币”，那是因为他们没看过本系列第一集，根本分不清什么是真正的“钱”，什么是“通货”。

cues.en: But I will correctly refer to it as base currency because it is not money. It is currency, and as we've learned, there is a big difference. Money has to be a store of value and maintain its purchasing power over long periods of time. We learned in Episode 1 that earlier in our history, our paper currency was just a claim check. It was a representation for real money of intrinsic value, the gold and silver that was held on deposit at the Treasury. You could walk into any bank,
cues.zh: 但我会准确地称其为“基础通货”，因为它根本不是钱。它只是通货，正如我们之前所学，这两者有天壤之别。钱必须能储藏价值，并在漫长的时间里保持购买力。我们在第一集学过，在历史早期，我们的纸币只是一种凭证，代表着存放在财政部、具有内在价值的真金白银。你可以走进任何一家银行，

cues.en: and slap your currency like, say, a $20 bill on the counter and redeem it for real money, a $20 gold piece. But now, this base currency that's piling up back here is really nothing but a receipt or a claim check on an IOU, that bond. So it's really nothing but a supply of numbers. The Treasury then deposits the newly created currency into the various branches of the government and the politicians say, hey, thanks for that. And the government does some deficit spending on public works,
cues.zh: 把通货——比如一张 20 美元纸币——拍在柜台上，换取真正的钱：一枚面值 20 美元的金币。但如今，堆在这里的这种基础通货，说白了只是一张借条（国债）的收据或兑换凭证罢了。所以它充其量就是一串数字供应。随后，财政部把这些凭空造出的通货存入政府各个部门，政客们纷纷表示笑纳。接着政府便开展赤字支出，投入到公共工程、

cues.en: social programs, and war. The government employees, contractors, and soldiers then deposit their pay in the banks. Now this may come as a shock to you, but when you deposit your currency with the bank, you're not actually depositing it into an account to be safely held in trust for you. Instead, you're actually loaning the bank your currency, and within certain legal limits, they can do with it pretty much anything they please. This includes gambling in the stock market,
cues.zh: 社会福利项目以及战争中。政府雇员、承包商和士兵随后将薪水存入银行。这可能会让你感到震惊：当你把钱存进银行时，并不是存进一个安全代管的账户里；相反，你实际上是把钱借给了银行。在一定法律限度内，他们几乎可以拿这笔钱做任何想做的事。这包括在股市里豪赌，

cues.en: and loaning it out at a profit, of course. Now this is where the machine of currency creation really gets cranking, because this is where something called fractional reserve lending comes into play. Fractional reserve lending is exactly what it says. The banks are allowed to reserve only a fraction of your deposit and loan the rest out. Although reserve ratios may vary, I'm going to use a 10% reserve ratio as our example. If you deposit $100 in your account,
cues.zh: 当然还有放贷牟利。到这一步，创造通货的机器才真正开足马力运转，因为所谓的“部分准备金贷款”登场了。部分准备金贷款名副其实：银行只需保留你存款的一小部分作为准备金，其余全都可以贷出去。尽管各家准备金率不尽相同，这里我们以 10% 为例。如果你在账户里存入 100 美元，

cues.en: the bank can legally take $90 of it and loan it out without telling you. The bank must hold $10 of your deposit in reserve just in case you want some of it. These reserves are called vault cash. But why does your bank account still say you have $100 if the bank has stolen $90 of it? Because the bank left IOUs it created, called bank credit, in its place. Now I know this sounds crazy, but here it is in black and white from the Fed.
cues.zh: 银行就可以在不通知你的情况下，合法地把其中的 90 美元借出去。银行只需保留 10 美元作为准备金，以防你提现，这部分准备金被称为“库存现金”。但既然银行挪走了 90 美元，为什么你的账户依然显示有 100 美元？因为银行在原地留下了一笔它自己造出来的借条，也就是“银行信用”。我知道这听起来匪夷所思，但美联储的文件里白纸黑字就是这么写的。

cues.en: Commercial banks create checkbook money when they grant a loan simply by adding new deposit dollars in accounts on their books in exchange for a borrower's IOU. These are nothing but numbers that the banks type into their computers. And even though these bank credit IOU numbers are very different from base currency numbers, because they only exist in computers, they are still currency, so now there is $190 in existence.
cues.zh: 商业银行在发放贷款时，只需在账目上增加新的存款金额来换取借款人的借据，便凭空创造出了支票货币。这些不过是银行敲进电脑里的数字。尽管这些银行信贷借据数字与基础货币截然不同——因为它们只存在于电脑中——但它们依然属于货币，所以现在市场上就有了190美元。

cues.en: Now the reason people take out loans from the banks is to buy something. They're going to buy a house or a car or something like that. So the borrower takes the $90 that the bank loaned to him from your account and he pays the seller of the item. But then the seller deposits that currency into his account and his bank loans out 90% of that and leaves bank credit numbers in its place.
cues.zh: 人们向银行贷款是为了买东西，比如买房、买车之类的。借款人拿着银行从你账户中贷给他的90美元，付给了卖家。但紧接着，卖家又把这笔钱存入自己的账户，他的银行又将其中的90%贷了出去，账面上只留下一串银行信贷数字。

cues.en: So now there's $271 in existence. This process repeats and repeats until under a 10% reserve ratio. An initial deposit of just $100 can create up to $1,000 of bank credit, all backed by $100 of vault cash, just 10%. But as I said, reserve ratios vary wildly. On some deposits it's 10%, on others it's 3%, and on some forms of the deposits reserve requirements are zero.
cues.zh: 所以现在就有了271美元。这个过程不断循环重复，在10%的准备金率下，最初区区100美元的存款，最多能创造出1000美元的银行信贷，而背后支撑的仅仅是金库里100美元的现金，刚好是10%。但正如我所说，准备金率差异极大，有些存款是10%，有些是3%，而在某些形式的存款中，准备金要求甚至为零。

cues.en: The result is that the expansion of the currency supply by the banks is far greater than even this example would lead you to believe. So once again, when currency is deposited in the banks, the banks get to lend it out, and then it gets redeposited and relent, redeposited and relent, redeposited and relent over and over again creating bank credit all the way. This is where the vast majority of our currency supply comes from. In fact, 92 to 96% of
cues.zh: 结果就是，银行对货币供应的扩张规模，远比这个例子让你以为的还要大得多。所以再次强调，货币存入银行后，银行贷出去，接着被重新存入、重新贷出，重新存入、重新贷出，如此循环往复，一路凭空创造着银行信贷。这就是我们绝大部分货币供应的来源。事实上，现存货币中高达92%到96%的……

cues.en: all currency in existence is created not by the government, but here in the banking system. Now, massive amounts of currency spewing into society may at first sound like a fun idea. That is, until you remember one of the most important hidden secrets of money from Episode 1. That the prices of everyday goods and services act as a sponge on an expanding currency supply. The more currency we have, the more prices rise. This is where inflation comes from.
cues.zh: ……所有货币都不是由政府创造的，而是在银行系统里诞生的。海量货币涌入社会，乍一听可能挺不错的。直到你想起第1集里关于货币最重要的隐藏秘密之一：日常商品和服务的价格就像海绵一样，吸收着膨胀的货币供应。货币越多，物价就涨得越高。这就是通货膨胀的由来。

cues.en: The true definition of inflation is an expansion of the currency supply. Rising prices are merely the symptom. So our entire currency supply is nothing but a couple of bucks whipped up in this hocus pocus scam where the Treasury and the Federal Reserve swap glorified IOUs, and a bunch of numbers that the banks just type into their computers. That's it. That's our entire currency supply. It's nothing but a supply of numbers, some of them printed, most of them typed, and there is nothing else.
cues.zh: 通货膨胀的真正定义，是货币供应的扩张。物价上涨只不过是表象。所以，我们全部的货币供应，无非就是财政部和美联储互换高级借据这出障眼法骗局里捣腾出来的几块钱，再加上银行敲进电脑里的一串数字。仅此而已。这就是我们全部的货币供应。它不过是一串数字的供给，一部分被印了出来，绝大部分是敲进电脑的，除此以外别无他物。

cues.en: But if you thought that was crazy, get ready to enter the twilight zone of modern economics. We work for some of that currency supply. True wealth is your time, but we trade away moments of our lives hour by hour, day by day, and year by year for numbers that somebody printed on pieces of paper or just typed into a computer. Now those numbers represent our blood, sweat, tears, labor, ideas, and talent. We are what gives the currency its value.
cues.zh: 但如果你觉得那已经够疯狂，那就准备好进入现代经济学的暮光地带。我们为其中一部分货币供给而工作。真正的财富是你的时间，可我们却一小时一小时、一天一天、一年一年地拿生命中的时刻，去换取某些人印在纸上、或直接敲进电脑里的数字。现在，那些数字代表着我们的血汗、眼泪、劳动、想法和才华。是我们让货币有了价值。

cues.en: But here comes the really cruel joke. We work hard so that we can save some of that currency, so that we can pay the tax collector in the United States as known as the IRS. They then turn it over to the Treasury so that the Treasury can pay the principal plus interest on that bond that the Federal Reserve bought with a check drawn on an account that has nothing in it. Now let's do a recap on this section because this is where the system begins to rob you and I on a massive scale.
cues.zh: 但真正残酷的笑话来了。我们努力工作，是为了攒下一些货币，好向美国的税务征收者——也就是IRS——缴税。然后他们把它交给财政部，好让财政部支付美联储用一张从空无一物的账户开出的支票所买债券的本金加利息。现在我们来回顾这一节，因为系统正是在这里开始大规模掠夺你和我。

cues.en: Much of our taxes are not used for schools, roads, and public services, but to pay interest on bonds that the Federal Reserve bought with a check drawn on an account that has nothing in it. The Federal Reserve is committing fraud. But here's one of the biggest secrets of them all. Before the establishment of the Federal Reserve, there was no need for personal income tax. The Federal Reserve was created in 1913, and that very same year,
cues.zh: 我们的税很多并不是用于学校、道路和公共服务，而是用来支付美联储用一张从空无一物的账户开出的支票所买债券的利息。美联储在搞欺诈。但最大的秘密之一在这里。在美联储成立之前，根本不需要个人所得税。美联储成立于1913年，而就在同一年，

cues.en: the Constitution was amended to allow income tax. Do you really think this was just a coincidence? Ask yourself how much income tax you've paid over your lifetime. Much of it has been silently siphoned away into the hands of those who own the system. Yes, this system has owners. Who they are is an even bigger secret that we'll get to shortly. But first, we need to understand the mumbo-jumbo of the so-called debt ceiling.
cues.zh: 宪法被修正，允许征收所得税。你真觉得这只是巧合吗？问问自己，你一生缴了多少所得税。其中大部分被悄悄抽走，落入拥有这个系统的人手中。是的，这个系统有主人。他们是谁是更大的秘密，我们很快会讲到。但首先，我们需要理解所谓债务上限的鬼话。

cues.en: It's all based on a huge paradox. There was interest due on that bond. And there was interest due on every one of those loans that the banks made. That means that there is interest due on every dollar in existence. Let me ask you something. If you borrow the very first dollar into existence, and that's the only dollar that exists on the planet, but you promise to pay it back plus another dollar's worth of interest,
cues.zh: 这一切都基于一个巨大的悖论。那张债券要付利息。银行发放的每一笔贷款也都要付利息。这意味着现存的每一美元都附带利息。我问你，如果你借出第一美元让它存在，而这是地球上唯一的一美元，但你承诺还本，并再付一美元等值的利息，

cues.en: Where do you get the second dollar to pay the interest? The answer is that you have to borrow that one into existence and promise to pay it back with interest as well. So now there are two dollars in existence, but you owe four and so on and so on. The result is there's never enough currency to pay the debt. There is always more debt in the system than there is currency in existence to pay the debt. Therefore, the whole system is impossible. It is finite.
cues.zh: 你从哪拿到第二美元来付利息？答案是，你得把那一美元也借出来让它存在，并同样承诺连本带利还回去。所以现在存在两美元，但你欠四美元，如此类推。结果是，永远没有足够货币来偿还债务。系统里的债务总是多于现存可用于偿债的货币。因此整个系统不可能成立。它是有限的。

cues.en: It will come to an end one day. What would happen if the government stopped borrowing to do deficit spending? Are the payments on those Treasury bonds going to stop? What would happen if the public stopped borrowing and going deeper into debt? Are your house and car payments going to stop? No. There is a payment due every month on the principal plus the interest on every dollar in existence and those payments do not stop. If we stop borrowing,
cues.zh: 这一切总有一天会走到尽头。如果政府不再借债来进行赤字支出，会发生什么？那些国债的偿付会停止吗？如果公众不再借贷、不再背负更多债务，又会发生什么？你的房贷和车贷会停下来吗？不会。现存的每一美元，每个月都要偿还本金和利息，而这些还款永远不会停止。如果我们停止借贷，

cues.en: then no new currency is created to replace the currency that we used to make those payments. Whether you're making a payment on a loan or paying tax to make a payment on a bond, the portion of the payment that goes to pay off the principal extinguishes that portion of the debt. But the debt also extinguishes the currency. Currency and debt are like matter and antimatter. When they meet, they annihilate each other. If we just pay off the principal only on all the loans and bonds that exist,
cues.zh: 就没有新的货币被创造出来，去填补用来还款消耗掉的货币。无论你是偿还贷款，还是缴税去偿还国债，用来还本金的那部分资金，在抵消债务的同时，也销毁了相应的货币。货币与债务就像物质与反物质。相遇之时，彼此湮灭。如果仅仅把所有现存贷款和债券的本金全部还清，

cues.en: the entire currency supply just vanishes. So if we don't go deeper into debt every year, look what happens. The whole thing goes into a deflationary collapse under the weight of those payments. Politicians and pundits alike talk about balancing the budget, paying down the debt, and living within our means. They don't understand that that is deflationary. It is impossible to do under our current monetary system without collapsing the whole economy.
cues.zh: 整个货币供应就会彻底消失。所以如果我们不是每年都在加深债务，看看会发生什么。整个体系都会在这些巨额还款的重压下，走向通缩性崩溃。政客和各路专家都在高谈阔论平衡预算、偿还债务、量入为出。他们根本不懂这会导致通缩。在现有的货币体系下，这样做必定会让整个经济崩盘。

cues.en: This is why any talk of a debt ceiling is not only ridiculous, it's delusional. The system is designed to require ever-increasing levels of debt just to continue. And that's why politicians will always kick the can down the road and raise this so-called debt ceiling over and over again until the whole system finally collapses under its own weight. In other words, they don't want it to collapse on their watch.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么大谈“债务上限”不仅荒唐，更是痴心妄想。这套体系的设计机制，决定了它必须靠不断推高的债务水平才能勉强维系。这也是为什么政客们总是在踢皮球，一次又一次地提高所谓的债务上限，直到整个系统最终不堪重负彻底崩塌。换句话说，他们只是不想让它在自己的任期内崩盘。

cues.en: The Founding Fathers of the United States knew the dangers of central banking and fought to free themselves from this very thing. The Revolutionary War started out as a tax revolt, but now we must pay tax just to have a monetary system. Having just suffered through the hyperinflation of the Continental Dollar, which was printed into oblivion to finance the Revolutionary War, they understood the dangers of fiat currency and debt-based monetary systems.
cues.zh: 美国的建国先父们深知央行制度的危险，并曾竭力摆脱它的控制。独立战争起初是一场抗税运动，而如今我们仅仅为了维持一套货币体系就不得不缴税。当年为了资助独立战争，大陆币被疯狂滥印直到沦为废纸，亲历过这种恶性通胀的先父们，深知法定货币和债务驱动型货币体系的致命危害。

cues.en: So to protect future generations from institutional theft and out-of-control government, they wrote into the Constitution that only gold and silver can be money for the simple fact that you can't print them. Our current system is not only unconstitutional, but it robs us of the liberty and prosperity our forefathers fought and died for. We are all feeling the effects of ignoring the Constitution right now. By forcing more currency into circulation,
cues.zh: 所以，为了保护后代免遭体制性掠夺和失控政府的侵害，他们把“唯有金银可作为法定货币”写入了宪法，原因很简单：金银无法凭空印制。我们现行的体系不仅违宪，更剥夺了先辈们浴血奋战换来的自由与繁荣。如今，我们所有人都在承受无视宪法的恶果。随着越来越多的货币被强行注入流通，

cues.en: our purchasing power is diluted. Inflation is a slow and insidious stealth tax that is simply the result of this debt-based monetary system. This system empowers and benefits those who create the currency and receive it first as they get to spend it into circulation before it has an effect on the economy. They're stealing purchasing power from you and transferring it to the banks and the government every hour of every day because of this false monetary system.
cues.zh: 我们的购买力被不断稀释。通货膨胀就是一种隐秘而阴险的隐形税，它是这种基于债务的货币体系的必然结果。这个体系赋权并造福了那些创造货币并最先拿到钱的人，因为他们能在货币对经济产生通胀冲击之前，就先把它花出去。正是这套虚假的货币体系，每时每刻都在窃取你的购买力，并将其转移给银行和政府。

cues.en: And it's not like the people at the top don't know this. To quote the Federal Reserve, the decrease in purchasing power incurred by the holders of money, due to inflation, imparts gains to the issuers of money. This is a fraud. It is a pyramid scheme. It is a Ponzi scheme. It's a scam. And it's a lie. Our entire monetary system is nothing but a form of legalized theft. But here's the biggest con job of them all.
cues.zh: 高层那些人并非对此一无所知。引用 Federal Reserve 的原话：通胀导致货币持有者的购买力下降，却为货币发行方带来了收益。这是彻头彻尾的欺诈，是传销，是庞氏骗局，是圈套，也是谎言。我们整个货币体系无非是一种合法的盗窃。但其中最大的骗局还在后头。

cues.en: The Federal Reserve is not federal, it has stockholders. There is no federal agency that has stockholders. What's a stockholder? A share of stock represents a percentage of ownership in a corporation. So the stockholders are the owners of that corporation. Therefore, the Federal Reserve is a private corporation with owners. And you can see it for yourself if you go to the Federal Reserve's website and it will say, the stockholders receive an annual dividend of 6%.
cues.zh: Federal Reserve 根本不是联邦机构，它有股东。没有任何联邦机构会有股东。什么是股东？一份股票代表一家公司一定比例的所有权。所以股东就是那家公司的所有者。因此，Federal Reserve 是一家拥有实际所有者的私营公司。如果你亲自去 Federal Reserve 的官网看一眼就会发现，上面写着：股东每年可获得 6% 的股息。

cues.en: Now, we know that the stock in the Federal Reserve was originally issued to the largest banks in the United States. But because of mergers and acquisitions through the years, you can't actually trace who owns the stock in the Federal Reserve. That's a very closely guarded secret. My guess would be that the owners are those primary dealers, the banks that get to make a profit by selling part of our national debt, those bonds, to the Federal Reserve, who buys them with a check from nothing.
cues.zh: 我们知道，Federal Reserve 的股票最初是发行给全美各大银行的。但由于多年来的兼并重组，你实际上根本无法查明究竟是谁持有着它的股票。这是个戒备森严的秘密。我推测所有者就是那些一级交易商——也就是那些靠把部分国债抛售给 Federal Reserve 来牟利的银行，而 Federal Reserve 则是凭空开出一张支票来买下这些债券。

cues.en: Then we pay tax to pay the principal and the interests on those bonds so that the Federal Reserve can pay the banks a 6% dividend. Don't be alarmed if you don't quite comprehend the deception of this system at first glance. Very few people do. It is purposely complex. The economist John Maynard Keynes once wrote,
cues.zh: 接着我们缴税来偿还这些债券的本金和利息，好让 Federal Reserve 能向那些银行支付 6% 的股息。如果你第一眼没完全看穿这套体系的骗局，千万别慌。极少有人能看懂。它是被故意设计得如此复杂的。经济学家 John Maynard Keynes 曾经写道：

cues.en: I believe that, presented correctly, anyone can understand this system regardless of how complex it is. So let's do a recap and break it down even more. The way the system works is that, step one, the government creates glorified IOUs. These bonds increase our national debt and put the public on the hook to pay it back. Step two, IOUs are swapped to create currency. The Treasury sells the bonds to the banks.
cues.zh: 我相信只要讲解得当，不管这套体系有多复杂，任何人都能够理解。那我们就来复盘一下，把它拆解得更透彻些。这套体系的运作方式是：第一步，政府制造出美化过的欠条。这些债券推高了国债，并把还债的重担强加给了公众。第二步，用欠条置换创造出货币。财政部将债券卖给银行。

cues.en: The banks then turn around and sell our national debt at a profit to the Federal Reserve, which they probably own. The Federal Reserve then opens its checkbook that doesn't have a penny in it and buys those IOUs with IOUs that it writes, checks, on a checking account that has a zero balance. Then they give those checks to the banks and currency just springs into existence. And then the whole process repeats.
cues.zh: 银行转头就把我们的国债加价卖给 Federal Reserve——而这家机构很可能本身就归它们所有。紧接着，Federal Reserve 拿出一本分文没有的支票簿，在一个余额为零的账户上开出支票——也就是用它自己写的欠条，买下了之前那些欠条。然后它们把支票交给银行，货币就这样凭空诞生了。接着，整个过程不断循环往复。

cues.en: This results in a build-up of bonds at the Federal Reserve and currency at the Treasury, which is really just a supply of numbers. The Treasury then deposits the numbers in the various branches of the government, and we get to Step 3. The government spends the numbers on promises, public works, social programs, and war. Then the government employees, contractors, and soldiers deposit their pay into the banks. And we get to Step 4.
cues.zh: 这导致美联储积累债券、财政部积累通货，而通货本质上只是数字供应。然后财政部把这些数字存入政府各部门，进入第3步。政府把这些数字花在承诺、公共工程、社会项目和战争上。接着政府雇员、承包商和士兵把工资存入银行。然后进入第4步。

cues.en: where the banks multiply the numbers by magically inventing more IOUs through fractional reserve lending, where they steal a portion of everyone's deposit and lend it out. That currency gets redeposited and then a portion is stolen again, and the process repeats over and over, magnifying the currency supply exponentially. Then we work for some of those numbers, which brings us to step five, where our numbers are taxed. We pay tax to the IRS,
cues.zh: 银行通过部分准备金贷款凭空发明更多借条，让这些数字成倍增加；它们偷走每个人存款的一部分再贷出去。这些通货被重新存入，然后一部分又被偷走，过程不断重复，使通货供应呈指数级放大。然后我们为其中一些数字工作，这就来到第5步：我们的数字被征税。我们向IRS缴税，

cues.en: who then turns our numbers over to the Treasury so the Treasury can pay the principal plus the interest on bonds that were purchased by the Federal Reserve with a check from nothing. Then we get to step six, the debt ceiling delusion. The system is designed to require ever increasing levels of debt and will eventually collapse under its own weight because politicians always kick the can down the road. They don't want it to collapse on their watch.
cues.zh: IRS再把我们的数字交给财政部，让财政部支付本金和利息；这些债券是美联储用一张凭空开出的支票买下的。然后进入第6步：债务上限的幻觉。这个制度被设计成需要不断增加的债务，最终会因自身重量而崩溃，因为政客总是把问题往后拖。他们不想在自己任内崩溃。

cues.en: And finally, step seven, the secret owners take their cut. The world's largest banks own the Federal Reserve. Those banks make a profit selling our national debt to the Fed. They make a profit when the Fed pays them interest on the reserves held at the Fed. And the Fed pays them a 6% dividend on their ownership of the Fed. This system is fundamentally evil. It funnels wealth from the working population to the government and the banking sector.
cues.zh: 最后是第7步：秘密所有者拿走他们的分成。全球最大的银行拥有美联储。这些银行把我们的国债卖给美联储来获利。当美联储就它们存放在美联储的准备金支付利息时，它们也获利。美联储还按它们对美联储的所有权支付6%的分红。这个制度从根本上就是邪恶的。它把财富从劳动大众输送给政府和银行部门。

cues.en: It is the cause of the artificial booms and busts of modern economies, and it causes great disparity of wealth between the rich and the working class. And it is only possible because we no longer use real money, we use currency. But worst of all, it is a form of enslavement. Bond is the root word of bondage. Whenever a government issues a bond, it is a promise to make us pay tax in the future.
cues.zh: 它是现代经济人为繁荣与萧条的原因，也造成富人与工人阶级之间巨大的财富差距。而它之所以可能，只是因为我们不再使用真正的货币，而是使用通货。但最糟糕的是，它是一种奴役形式。Bond（债券）是bondage（奴役）的词根。每当政府发行债券，就是在承诺让我们在未来缴税。

cues.en: Nobody asked you if you wanted to pay tax today for the prosperity we all enjoyed in the last century. Nobody is asking our children if they want to work hard in the future to pay for the prosperity we're enjoying now. George Washington once wrote to James Madison, No generation has the right to contract debts greater than can be paid off during the course of its own existence. By stealing prosperity from tomorrow so we can spend it today, we enslave ourselves
cues.zh: 没人问过你，是否愿意今天缴税，来支付我们上世纪共同享受的繁荣。也没人问我们的孩子，是否愿意在未来努力工作，来支付我们现在享受的繁荣。George Washington曾写信给James Madison：“没有任何一代人有权背负超过其自身存续期间能够偿清的债务。”我们偷走明天的繁荣来供今天挥霍，就是在奴役自己

cues.en: and future generations. Now this all sounds pretty bad, but there is great hope, for you are the greatest threat to this false monetary system. This system relies on the public being ignorant of its workings. Please share this knowledge with everyone you know, because an informed public that fully understands the system can build a better future for generations to come. And now I leave you with this quote, widely attributed to a former director of the Bank of England.
cues.zh: 以及子孙后代。现在这一切听起来很糟，但仍有很大希望，因为你就是这个虚假货币体系的最大威胁。这个体系依赖公众对其运作方式一无所知。请把这一知识分享给你认识的每个人，因为一个充分理解该体系、知情的公众，能为后代建设更美好的未来。最后，我以这句话作结，它被广泛认为是Bank of England一位前董事所言。

cues.en: The modern banking system manufactures money out of nothing. The process is perhaps the most astounding piece of sleight of hand that was ever invented. Banking was conceived in inequity and born in sin. Bankers own the earth. Take it away from them, but leave them the power to create money and control credit, and with the flick of a pen, they will create enough money to buy it back again. But if you want to continue as the slaves of bankers and pay the cost of your own slavery,
cues.zh: 现代银行体系凭空制造货币。这个过程也许是有史以来最令人震惊的障眼法。银行业孕育于不公，诞生于罪恶。银行家拥有整个世界。把世界从他们手中夺走，但留给他们创造货币和控制信贷的权力，他们只需动笔一挥，就能创造出足够的钱把它再买回来。但如果你还想继续做银行家的奴隶，并为自己受奴役买单，

cues.en: Let them continue to create money and to control credit. This is the Federal Reserve in Washington, D.C. It's located on Constitution Street, and that is just as much of a joke as the New York Fed being located on Liberty Street. Both of them are unconstitutional, both of them limit our liberty, and they transfer wealth away from us every second of every day to the Federal Reserve, to the government, and to the banking sector.
cues.zh: 那就让他们继续创造货币、控制信贷吧。这里是华盛顿特区的美联储。它坐落在宪法街，而这就跟纽约联储坐落在自由街一样，是个十足的笑话。这两者都违宪，都限制我们的自由，而且每天每一秒都在把财富从我们手中转移给美联储、政府和银行业。

cues.en: You are now among the one in a million who can detect the theft of your prosperity. So the big question is, what can you do about it? One, watch this video until you can describe and teach it to others. Those who understand this system can make preparations for its unavoidable collapse and protect themselves. History shows that those who don't will probably be wiped out. Two, share this video with everyone, especially those you care about.
cues.zh: 你现在已经属于百万分之一，能够察觉自己的繁荣正被偷走的人。那么关键问题是，你能做些什么？第一，把这个视频看到你能向别人描述并讲解为止。理解这个体系的人，可以为它不可避免的崩溃做准备并保护自己。历史表明，不理解的人很可能会被淘汰。第二，把这个视频分享给所有人，尤其是你关心的人。

cues.en: All it takes is a mouse click or two to get this message in front of millions. Post this video on Facebook, tweet it, email it to loved ones. Please share it wherever you can. Three, join the conversation. The current world monetary system is based on a 300-year-old design meant to enrich a few at the expense of the many. There must be a better way.
cues.zh: 只需点一两下鼠标，就能让这条信息出现在数百万人面前。把视频发到 Facebook，发推文，电邮给你爱的人。请尽可能到处分享。第三，加入讨论。当前世界货币体系基于一套有 300 年历史的设计，目的是以多数人的利益为代价让少数人致富。一定存在更好的方式。

cues.en: We've created an open source platform for the design and development of a new world monetary system. We're calling on every economist, every student, every college, every bright mind, and anyone who cares to join the discussion. In educating ourselves and each other, we can prevent the further loss of our freedoms and maybe, just maybe, win some of them back.
cues.zh: 我们创建了一个开源平台，用于设计和开发新的世界货币体系。我们呼吁每一位经济学家、每一位学生、每一所大学、每一个聪明头脑，以及任何愿意加入讨论的人。通过教育自己和彼此，我们可以防止自由进一步流失，也许，只是也许，还能赢回其中一部分。

cues.en: Your episode four is very beneficial, very helpful. It's going to introduce these ideas to a lot of people. And like I've just been talking about, we have to change people's mind. And the more they understand it, the better. And I think we're at this point now where more people in the last several years, four or five years, have thought about the Fed than they ever have in the previous 95 years. So I think an explanation and...
cues.zh: 你们的第四集非常有益，非常有帮助。它会把这些想法介绍给很多人。就像我刚才说的，我们必须改变人们的想法。他们越理解，就越好。我认为我们现在到了这个节点：过去四五年里，思考美联储的人比此前 95 年里任何时候都多。所以我认为，一个解释和……

cues.en: diagrams to show it is very helpful because quite frankly they're not going to get it in their grade school, they're not going to get it in their high schools, they're not going to get it in...
cues.zh: 用图表来展示它非常有帮助，因为坦白说，他们在小学里学不到这些，在高中里也学不到，在……里也学不到……

cues.en: college unless they're in a very rare circumstance to understand how this works. You know, for years before I got involved in really studying gold and some of the things I write and talk about today, I was a monetary economist for decades. You know, in your video you talk about the primary dealers. I was chief counsel and chief credit officer, one of the largest primary dealers for 10 years. So I had an inside seat on the Treasury market and have the privilege of working with several
cues.zh: 除非情况极特殊，否则在大学里根本搞不懂这是怎么运作的。在真正深入研究黄金、撰写并讨论如今这些话题之前，我做了数十年的货币经济学家。你在视频里提到了“一级交易商”。我曾在这类最大的一级交易商之一担任了十年的首席法律顾问兼首席信贷官。所以我对国债市场有着一手内幕视角，并有幸与几位……

cues.en: former vice chairman of the Board of Governors, Manly Johnson and David Mullins, going back to the 80s and 90s. So I'm very immersed in what you were talking about. I thought it was extremely accurate, extremely clear. I didn't think you were stretching on any points. It was really something out of a...
cues.zh: 80、90年代的美联储前副主席 Manly Johnson 和 David Mullins 共事。所以我对你所讲的内容深有共鸣。我认为讲得极其精准、极其透彻。没有任何夸大其词的成分。这完全就是一堂……

cues.en: PhD course, except that it was very easy to understand. I think it's accessible. I think we're seeing a little bit of a revolution in communications in the following sense. As you point out, the Fed was created in 1913. Well, in 1913, there was no web, there was no YouTube, no Twitter. There was really no one to kind of stand up and oppose the Fed or call them out, if you will, or really get into a discussion that everyday Americans could follow. That's not true now with social media and everything else.
cues.zh: 博士级别的课程，但却极其通俗易懂。我觉得它非常接地气。从某种意义上说，我们正在见证一场信息传播的革命。正如你所指出的，美联储成立于 1913 年。而在 1913 年，没有网络，没有 YouTube，也没有 Twitter。根本没有人能站出来反对美联储，或者去公开叫板，甚至展开一场普通美国人都能跟上的讨论。但如今有了社交媒体等一切工具，情况截然不同了。
